mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate directly reduces the risk-free rate, lowering the discount rate for equity valuation models and increasing the present value of future cash flows, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in low-rate environments are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year CPI inflation rate exceeds 3.0%, it triggers a market expectation of aggressive monetary tightening, which initially causes a sell-off in equities as investors price in higher discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 3.0% (y/y) over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which triggers a negative earnings outlook for the S&P 500, resulting in negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative returns (Rank IC < 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a low-unemployment regime (UNRATE < 4.0%), the labor market tightness leads to wage pressures and inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates, which subsequently depresses equity valuations and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in > 60% of periods when UNRATE < 4.0% over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates robust economic activity and corporate profitability, which supports higher equity valuations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO growth fails to predict positive returns (Rank IC < 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1,500,000 units, it signals a contraction in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of reduced consumer spending and economic slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of instances when HOUST < 1500.0 over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and a rise in CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicates a monetary policy response to high inflation, which typically leads to a negative equity market reaction due to higher discount rates and reduced growth expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint increase in FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL fails to predict negative returns (Rank IC < 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (GDPC1 growth rate > 2.5% annually), the economy is approaching its potential, leading to a higher probability of a recession, which causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate a slowdown.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in > 60% of periods when GDPC1 growth > 2.5% (annualized) over the last 5 years.
